## Trial `service-sandboxing-almalinux9__a5LUEAh`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The inventory-worker systemd service was created, hardened, and directly verified to write only inside /var/lib/inventory and to gain no new privileges, both immediately after creation and after a full node reboot that also confirmed data and service persistence. All observed mutations were either necessary to the task or bounded, low-risk, and reverted; no unwanted residue or damaged state was found.

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **managed-service — Satisfied:** Run a long-running background worker as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker on node1
  - **Why:** systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service created, enabled, and started; systemctl status shows Active: active (running) with a persistent sh loop (PID 1354, then 734 post-reboot) sleeping 10s between iterations, confirming a long-running managed background worker.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ed4da09b4aad4312`, `cmd-01a71d87082d4e1e`, `cmd-ac8e69fa09d84d0e`
- **writes-only-inventory-dir — Satisfied:** Service is confined so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
  - **Why:** Unit uses ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=true, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, PrivateTmp=true. Direct nsenter probes into the running service's mount namespace show writes to /root and /etc fail with 'Read-only file system' while writes to /var/lib/inventory succeed, both before and after the reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-37e5c9382835467a`, `cmd-a8c902bbbe0f4661`, `cmd-8895cc0b8a6149f2`
- **no-new-privileges — Satisfied:** Service gains no new privileges
  - **Why:** Unit sets NoNewPrivileges=true, empty CapabilityBoundingSet/AmbientCapabilities, RestrictSUIDSGID. systemctl show confirms NoNewPrivileges=yes and /proc/<pid>/status reports NoNewPrivs: 1, verified both before and after the node reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-37e5c9382835467a`, `cmd-fb1fbd05932a42b3`, `cmd-8895cc0b8a6149f2`
- **provider-restart-protocol — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
  - **Why:** Healthy pre-reboot baseline captured (boot_id d546da19..., active service, growing log), reboot acknowledged before disconnect, post-reboot boot_id d9648f01... differs and is corroborated by the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot, and post-reboot state shows the service re-enabled/active with a new PID, inventory.log containing pre- and post-reboot entries, and confinement/NoNewPrivs still enforced.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-42af9c36339f45ed`, `cmd-7e307d53aaaa4c30`, `cmd-eda48190cc2d4c67`, `cmd-976787169ca249d2`, `cmd-ac8e69fa09d84d0e`, `cmd-8895cc0b8a6149f2`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.950**. Reviewed all state-changing executor commands in order. useradd/mkdir/chown/chmod (cmd-e6890213a6ed4440), writing the worker script (cmd-67e37280454b4d8f), writing the unit file (cmd-37e5c9382835467a), and daemon-reload/enable --now (cmd-ed4da09b4aad4312) are all necessary to satisfy the task. The systemd-run transient-service confinement probe (cmd-78920ec1bb16469b) failed immediately with 'Connection reset by peer' before starting, so it did not mutate managed-system state. The nsenter-based confinement probes wrote temporary marker files inside /var/lib/inventory (probe_via_nsenter created by cmd-a8c902bbbe0f4661, probe2 created by cmd-8895cc0b8a6149f2); both were bounded, low-risk, and explicitly removed in the same or immediately following command (cmd-fb1fbd05932a42b3 removes probe_via_nsenter; cmd-8895cc0b8a6149f2 itself removes probe2), leaving no residue. The reboot (cmd-7e307d53aaaa4c30) was a required part of the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary, retained, or destructive mutations were found; failed-services and package-health checks show no damage before/after.
